title: Pointwise smoothness from etale-local Artinian lifts
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], and let $x\in|X|$ [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose that for every surjection $B'\twoheadrightarrow B$ of Artinian local rings with square-zero kernel and every commutative diagram $\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{a}X$, $\operatorname{Spec}B'\xrightarrow{c}S$ with $a$ sending the unique point to $x$, there is an etale covering $\{T_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B'\}$ and maps $T_i\to X$ over $S$ restricting to $a$ on $T_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B'}\operatorname{Spec}B$. Here Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize, and local means having a unique maximal ideal. Then $x$ has an open neighbourhood $V\subset X$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] on which $f$ is smooth, with smoothness tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Tag 0APN, lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point, Artinian small-extension test; Tag 04AM, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth, and the preceding discussion of the equivalent etale-local lifting convention. The etale-local Artinian form is the pointwise variant, with obstruction vanishing descended along the etale cover.

proof.text: Fix a test from the hypothesis, and put $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}B'$ and $I=\ker(B'\to B)$. The quotient presentation identifies $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ with the affine first order thickening defined by $I$, since $I^2=0$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-infinitesimal-lift-pseudotorsor] to $f:X\to S$, $j$, $a$ and $c$. It supplies a quasi-coherent module $H$ on $T$ and a sheaf $\mathcal L$ of compatible lifts, with a simply transitive action of $H_{\mathrm{et}}$ wherever a lift exists. The given etale covering and its lifts give local sections of $\mathcal L$. Translation by each such section identifies the restricted lift sheaf with $H_{\mathrm{et}}$ there. Thus $\mathcal L$ is an $H_{\mathrm{et}}$-torsor in the general abelian-sheaf sense of [def-sc-gm-torsor].

source.place: Tags 061A (lemma-sheaf), 061C (lemma-action-sheaf), 061D (remark-special-case); Tag 04AM (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), proof, torsor steps (I) and (II).

proof.text: The scheme $T$ is affine and $H$ is quasi-coherent, so [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] gives $H^1(T_{\mathrm{et}},H_{\mathrm{et}})=0$. By [lem-sc-torsor-h1], the torsor $\mathcal L$ is isomorphic to the trivial torsor $H_{\mathrm{et}}$. The image of its zero section is a section of $\mathcal L(T)$. By the definition of $\mathcal L$, this is a map $\gamma:T\to X$ with $\gamma j=a$ and $f\gamma=c$. We have therefore obtained an actual global lift for every centered Artinian square-zero test in the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 03P2 (theorem-zariski-fpqc-quasi-coherent), affine case; torsor classification: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1).

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme chart $q:U\to X$ and a point $u\in U$ over $x$, using the atlas in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Write $g=fq:U\to S$. By the chart definition [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], applied with the identity chart of $S$, $g$ is locally of finite presentation. The calculus [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] gives that $g$ is locally of finite type and that $q$, being etale, is smooth. Algebraic spaces here are viewed as stacks with only identity arrows, so these representable-morphism laws apply.

source.place: Tag 0APN (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point), proof, choice of etale scheme charts; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0410 (lemma-finite-presentation-local).

proof.text: Consider any Artinian local square-zero test for $g$ at $u$, with $b:T_0\to U$, $c:T\to S$ and $gb=cj$. The map $qb$ sends the unique point of $T_0$ to $x$, so step 2 gives $\gamma:T\to X$ with $\gamma j=qb$ and $f\gamma=c$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-affine-infinitesimal-lift] to the smooth map $q:U\to X$, the affine first order thickening $j$, and the maps $b$ and $\gamma$, all over the scheme $S$. It gives $\delta:T\to U$ with $\delta j=b$ and $q\delta=\gamma$. Then $g\delta=fq\delta=f\gamma=c$. Consequently every such test for the scheme map $g$ has a global lift.

source.place: Tag 0APN (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point), proof, transfer of tests to a chart; Tag 04AM (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), smooth implies affine infinitesimal lifting.

proof.text: In particular step 4 solves every small-extension test for $g$ at $u$: [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point] states that these are Artinian local extensions with length-one kernel and in particular square-zero kernel. Its other hypotheses hold: $S$ is locally Noetherian and $g$ is locally of finite type by step 3. That criterion gives that $g$ is smooth at $u$. Now [lem-sfb-space-smooth-source-point-locality] applies to $f$ and the smooth map $q$ from step 3. Since $g=fq$, it implies that $f$ is smooth at $q(u)=x$. The same cited statement defines smoothness at a point as smoothness on an open neighbourhood; hence it supplies the required open subspace $V\subset X$ containing $x$.
